title: land refuses to remove a finished worker's worktree when the clone it runs in is itself a linked worktree, so the autopilot runner's workers are never cleaned up
goal: bl_land's worker-worktree cleanup judges a worktree under the clone by the git COMMON dir's parent (path.parent != common.parent/.claude/worktrees), so when land runs in a clone that is itself a linked worktree (the autopilot runner's worktree is one; so was mac-sixth's wt-sixth) every worker worktree under that clone's own .claude/worktrees is called 'not under .claude/worktrees/ of the clone' and land stops at step branch; a worker named by its item id, not agent-*, is also refused as not a worker's. Fix: the clone is git rev-parse --show-toplevel of the directory land runs in; a clean, process-free worktree under THAT clone's .claude/worktrees on the item's own work/<id> branch is removed by land whether it is named agent-* or by the item id, locked by a Claude Code agent or not; a worktree anywhere else, one with uncommitted changes, a live process, or on another item's branch is still kept with its reason. Planted tests (name land_removes_worker_worktree_of_a_linked_clone): a linked-worktree clone with the worker under its own .claude/worktrees is removed, one under the main checkout's directory from a different linked clone is kept, a dirty one is kept. Found by mac-sixth landing BG-thez4izx: the autopilot's runner clone is linked, so without this its workers' worktrees are never removed.

run: import sys; sys.exit(0 if 'common.parent.joinpath(*WORKER_DIR)' not in open('_tools/bl_land.py').read() else 1)

repro_reason: the defect is which directory counts as the clone; the match shows the ownership check no longer takes the git common dir's parent
